Balangauan and Zaragosa will be driven not only by the desire to avenge their recent setbacks but also by the confidence that comes with playing on familiar turf. Pueblo de Oro's rolling terrain, deep natural ravines and five interconnected lakes provide a demanding test, but one that the local players know perhaps better than anyone in the field. That familiarity could prove especially valuable in a format where teamwork, strategy and momentum can be just as decisive as individual shot-making. Sarines, teaming up with twin sister Mona, Rafa Anciano and Kendra Garingalao, will likewise have ample opportunity to get acquainted with the Robert Trent Jones Jr.-designed layout before the matches begin. But Balangauan and Zaragosa will have the added advantage of rediscovering the lines, breaks and nuances of a course they call home. Cebuanas Apple Gotiong and Lois Lane Go will provide further depth to Team South, joining Balangauan and Zaragosa in anchoring the region's bid to wrest the championship from the North in the three match-play formats – Fourball (Best-Ball), Foursomes (alternate shot) and singles. And there is unfinished business to settle. Team South is out to avenge its loss at The Country Club last year, when the Northerners fashioned out a commanding 26 1/2-21 1/2 victory in the inaugural staging. This time, the venue has been switched to Pueblo de Oro as part of organizing Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc.'s commitment to fair play and sportsmanship, giving the South not only home-course familiarity but also a fresh setting in which to turn the tables. The change of scenery, however, hardly guarantees a change in fortunes. And while the girls' 15-18 division may provide the headline attraction, it will hardly be the only one worth watching. The Finals will also feature the 7-10 and 11-14 boys' and girls' divisions, as well as the boys' 15-18 category, bringing together a deep pool of the country's most promising young players in a format designed to showcase both individual talent and team spirit.

Safety measures tightened for 4th Southeast Open Water Swimming meet. Local organizers will implement optimum measures for the safety, security and well-being of swimmers in the 4th Southeast Asia Open Water Swimming Championships presented by the Philippine Sports Commission from Aug. 21 to 23 at the Boracay Newcoast in Malay, Aklan. “The safety of all our athletes is our top priority now, ensuring they will have a secure and safety environment during the competition,” said Philippine Aquatics Inc. vice president Jojo Quilop following the recent interagency coordinating meeting for the event. “What PAI and the local organizing committee have done is submit a comprehensive plan to Asia Aquatics on the safety protocols, including how many kayaks, rubber life boats and jet skis that will be required for the meet, for its approval” Quilop revealed. “We also are looking at whatever loopholes that are left so that our safety measures are airtight,” said the PAI official, adding that they also will also be supported by the Philippine Coast Guard and Philippine National Police once the regional open water showcase unfolds. “Meetings with the provincial risk reduction and management officials of Aklan have taken place while next week we will have another meeting with the municipal risk reduction and management officials,” he said. Quilop noted that the inaugural international open water swimming meet that the country will host would be within the popular resort island’s cove “so that the waters and weather will be calmer compared to the other side of Boracay.” Supplementing these measures, he said, was the assistance of Philippine Lifesaving, which will send five highly-trained lifeguard daily while the races are going on. “One of Philippine Lifesaving’s 68 centers nationwide is in Boracay so we will send five volunteer lifeguards daily during the competition to supplement and complement whatever safety requirements that are needed by the organizers,” Philippine Lifesaving secretary general DJ Salonga said. “All of these lifeguard volunteers have undergone intensive training and awarded Philippine Lifesaving certificates for undergoing our lifesaving course,” Salonga stressed. “We are only to glad offer our help for this international open water swimming event.” Quilop said that besides the safety measures for participants of the 4th Southeast Asia Open Water Swimming Championships “we are also taking steps in preserving and protecting the ecological and marine environment while we are there.” “We are conscious of Boracay’s reputation as top tourist destination of our country,” he said,” so we want to maintain that status.” “This is the first time the Philippine will host the 4th Southeast Asia Ope Water Swimming Championships and we want to maintain the of everyone while having a good time with us. We want this to be the best hosting. “The idea of PAI is that this will be just the first of many more international open water swimming events considering that we have 7,100 islands all over the country.”

Lucky Beauty and Paulash combine their expertise in a new eye makeup collaboration. The Filipino beauty industry is having its moment. As local brands gain attention beyond the country, Filipino-made beauty products are increasingly being recognized for their quality, creativity, and ability to compete in a growing international market. But as the industry continues to expand, there is still plenty of room for local players to grow together. One example is the latest collaboration between Lucky Beauty and Paulash, two homegrown beauty brands bringing their respective expertise together to create an eye makeup collection. Lucky Beauty, the makeup brand co-founded by actress Andrea Brillantes, has teamed up with local cluster lash brand Paulash for a collaboration designed to make creating an eye look easier. Launched last Aug. 6 at Nada Conceptions in Makati City, the collection features six shades of the Multiuse Eyeshadow Wand, which can be used on the eyes, as contour, or as a highlighter, alongside six custom-designed cluster lashes. For Paolo Salapatan, Lucky Beauty’s co-founder and managing partner, the partnership was also a way to challenge the usual formula for beauty collaborations. “I didn't wanna do the usual fashion brand or whatever,” he told Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. “I was just like, we're here to challenge ourselves. How can you push the envelope further?” Instead of developing its own lashes, Lucky Beauty chose to work with Paulash because of the latter's expertise in the category. “We could've done this ourselves. We could've done our own lashes. But I didn't choose to do it, we are not experts at that,” he said. While Lucky Beauty considers itself an expert in makeup, Paolo said Paulash brought the expertise needed for lashes. The partnership also aims to introduce more consumers to cluster lashes, which he believes can help expand the local beauty market. “For such a young industry like F-Beauty, not all people use lashes,” he said. “We chose to do a collaboration to help develop the market, to help teach people that cluster lashes are pretty easy, they're nice to look at.” For Paulash chief marketing officer Abigail Justine Semillano, CEO of Rio Rebel Group (Paulash and Burvon), the partnership was an easy decision. Andrea has been a longtime Paulash customer, even before her own lash collection existed. “She's always been an OG user of Paulash,” she said. “For someone who's been patronizing our product right from the start, of course, no questions asked. We're down to do a collaboration.” Beyond the products, both brands see the partnership as an opportunity for the local beauty industry to explore more collaborations. Abby described it as an “opportunity opener and eye opener” for other Filipino beauty brands to combine their resources, expertise, and specialties. For Paolo, the collaboration is ultimately about giving customers the best products possible, even if that means working with a brand that could otherwise be considered a competitor. “It's about how we can best deliver the best products to our customers,” he said. The partnership also reflects how Lucky Beauty itself is evolving. He shared that the brand is reworking some of its original offerings while exploring new categories as Andrea matures. “Wherever she goes, we go,” he said, adding that consumers can expect the brand to mature and explore other things alongside its muse. For the rest of 2026, Lucky Beauty plans to continue expanding its offerings, moving from eyes to lips and eventually back to face products. The brand is also preparing five new perfume scents this year. Meanwhile, Paulash is gearing up for a busier fourth quarter. Abby said the brand has been working behind the scenes and will be making more noise in the local beauty scene, giving lash enthusiasts more to look forward to. Together, Lucky Beauty and Paulash are showing that as Filipino beauty continues to gain attention, collaboration can be another way for local brands to strengthen the industry and give consumers more reasons to discover homegrown products.

‘No-build zone’ declared in Baguio landslide ground zero. BAGUIO CITY – Mayor Benjamin Magalong announced the declaration of a "no-build zone" at ground zero of Barangay Guisad Surong, after severe landslides buried three houses and killed 10 people at the height of the southwest monsoon in Baguio City. According to Magalong, affected residents will not be allowed to return to live or build houses because there are signs of soil instability observed by city engineers. “I had our engineers go to the landslide area and they saw that the soil is too stressed, so it is dangerous to live in. And for the displaced residents, the DSWD (Department of Social Welfare and Development) promised to first cover the rental support for their relocation and we will also arrange for them to find relocation sites,” Magalong said. It was learned that more than 20 families affected by the Guisad Surong landslide are temporarily staying at the Baguio International Academy. Residents were banned from returning to the area. The city government promised to find temporary rental houses for the affected families while working on a permanent relocation site. According to Magalong, DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian promised that the agency will assume the ₱10,000 monthly rental fee for three to six months while long-term socialized housing is being arranged. He said he has also coordinated with the concerned agencies, especially with the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), to revisit the area for a clean-up drive and assess the area and identify engineering solutions to help prevent similar incidents. Magalong said the Baguio city government continues to lead the local response, coordinating relief operations and working with national government agencies to address the immediate needs of affected families. Magalong previously revealed that there was also a landslide in the area in the 1970s, just next to the area where the deadly landslide struck on Sunday.

Pag-IBIG Fund, Avida and Amaia join hands to expand homeownership for Filipino workers. Pag-IBIG Fund, Avida Land Corp. and Amaia Land Corp. signed a memorandum of understanding to expand quality housing choices for Filipino workers under President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino Program. The partnership will explore special rates on identified homes that qualified members may finance through Pag-IBIG Housing Loans of up to ₱10 million. The agreement forms part of continuing efforts by the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development and Pag-IBIG Fund to strengthen partnerships with private developers. Pag-IBIG Fund recently increased its maximum housing loan amount to ₱10 million per borrower and invited more leading developers to have their projects accredited and made accessible to qualified members through Pag-IBIG financing. DHSUD Secretary Jose Ramon P. Aliling said the partnership advances the Marcos administration’s efforts to expand homeownership through stronger government support and private-sector participation. “We continue to heed the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to expand homeownership through stronger collaboration between government and the private sector. By helping developers connect their available housing inventory with Pag-IBIG Fund members and affordable financing, we give more Filipino workers quality housing choices within their means while supporting a stronger housing sector,” Aliling said. He added that closer cooperation with private developers also supports DHSUD’s efforts to facilitate their compliance with the balanced housing development requirement, helping generate more socialized housing projects and expand the supply of affordable homes. Pag-IBIG Fund has introduced financing measures that serve members across different income segments. Qualified borrowers under socialized housing may avail themselves of a subsidized interest rate of 3%, while members purchasing homes above the socialized housing ceiling may benefit from promotional rates of 4.5% or 5.75%, depending on the loan amount. With its higher loan ceiling of ₱10 million, the agency is expanding affordable financing not only for socialized housing borrowers but also for middle-income Filipino workers seeking homes that suit their needs and financial capacity. Avida and Amaia are residential brands of Ayala Land. The partnership builds on Ayala Land’s commitment to expanding access to quality homes across different segments of the market, while strengthening collaboration with government and other stakeholders to make homeownership more accessible to Filipino families. Avida Land President Raquel S. Cruz said Pag-IBIG Fund’s competitive housing loan rates and higher loan ceiling provide Avida and Amaia greater opportunities to serve more Pag-IBIG members. “Our longstanding partnership with Pag-IBIG Fund has helped make homeownership possible for many Filipino families. With its competitive housing loan rates and increased loan ceiling of up to ₱10 million, we see an even greater opportunity for Avida and Amaia to serve more middle- and upper-middle-income members and pursue further synergies that will help more Filipinos own quality homes,” Cruz said. The parties will also explore the registration and accreditation of identified Avida and Amaia projects for Developer-Assisted housing loan processing, including qualified Amaia projects under Expanded 4PH. They will study measures to streamline documentation, loan processing and the release of proceeds, while assisting prospective buyer-borrower-beneficiaries in meeting program requirements. Pag-IBIG Fund Chief Executive Officer Marilene C. Acosta said the agency continues to work with a growing number of trusted developers to provide members with more quality housing choices and make homeownership more affordable. “At Pag-IBIG Fund, we understand that every member has different housing needs and financial capacities. In line with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s directive to expand homeownership, we are working with a growing number of trusted developers to bring our members more quality housing choices and special offers. By combining these with our affordable rates and housing loans of up to ₱10 million, we hope to help our members find homes they can comfortably afford, with monthly payments that may be comparable to or even lower than rent. In this way, their hard-earned money goes toward a home they can truly call their own and a better future for their families,” Acosta said. Acosta, Cruz and Amaia Land Vice President Aris C. Gonzales signed the agreement, with Aliling and Ayala Land President and CEO Meean B. Dy serving as witnesses. Also present were Pag-IBIG Fund Deputy Chief Executive Officers Alexander Hilario G. Aguilar, Robert John S. Cosico, Benjamin R. Felix Jr. and Marcial C. Pimentel, along with other senior officers.

Abra, Batangas hold lead as Cebu trounces Ilagan-Isabela. Defending champion Abra Solid North and Batangas City beat their opponents on Wednesday, Aug. 12, to keep top spot in their divisions in the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) 2026 Season at the Batangas City Coliseum. The Abra Weavers routed the Bulacan Kuyas, 110-84, in the first game, while the Batangas City Tanduay Athletics thwarted the Imus Yangkees, 88-80, in the nightcap of another triple-bill in the round-robin elimination phase of the two-division, 26-team tournament. Abra extended its winning run to 17 and climbed to a 19-1 record in the North division, ahead of San Juan (16-2), Caloocan (17-3) and Ilagan Isabela (13-8) in the chase for playoff spots. Batangas quelled Imus' final rally to rise to 16-3 in the South division, where it towed Quezon Province (13-3), Binan (17-4), Gensan (15-4) and Cebu (17-5). The Cebu Greats trounced the Ilagan Isabela Cowboys, 80-52, in the second game to keep in line for a top 4 finish and the homecourt advantage that goes with it in the quarterfinal playoffs. Mark Meneses led Cebu with 14 points and 11 rebounds, followed by Wowie Escosio with 10 points and 6 rebounds, homegrown Elmer Echavez with 9 points and 3 rebounds, and Cebuano legend Dondon Hontiveros with 9 points, all from triples. Simon Camacho was chosen the SportsPlus best player, however, with an all-around 6 points, 17 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 blocks and 1 steal. Impressive as the Greats were, Camacho warned they could play even better. "I feel this isn't our best yet. This team has something more to offer," said the 6-foot-5 Camacho. Only Jayboy Solis hit his stride for the Cowboys with 10 points and 3 rebounds, while Arth Dela Cruz settled for 6 points, 14 rebounds, 7 assists and 2 blocks. Dave Ildefonso, the reigning MVP, posted 23 points, 7 assists and 2 rebounds to capture his fifth straight best player honors for Abra. Alfred Batino supported with 13 points and 6 rebounds; Raven Gonzales, last year's top rookie, contributed 13 points and 4 rebounds; Jake Figueroa chalked up 10 points, 7 assists, 5 steals and 4 rebounds; and 6-foot-8 Drex Delos Reyes carded 10 points plus 2 rebounds. The Weavers dominated both boards, 47-30, and exploited this advantage to outscore the Kuyas, 72-26, in the paint. Bulacan slipped to 5-16 despite Benedict Benedictos' 29 points, laden with nine triples, 3 assists and 2 rebounds, Andrei Acop's 12 points and 7 rebounds, and Jeremy Cruz's 12 points and 2 assists. Batangas led as far as 63-38, midway through the third quarter, but Imus turned hot in the fourth and threatened, 78-81, after back-to-back triples by Dylan Darbin and Meray Merada. Batangas' Ino Comboy, however, drilled in a triple and Oliver Arim drove in to seal the outcome, 86-78, with 41.3 seconds left. Rhinwill Yambing paced Batangas with 18 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists, Cedrick Ablaza with 12 points, 12 rebounds and 2 assists, homegrown Nikki Perez with 11 points and 4 rebounds, and Jhan Nermal with 9 points, 9 rebounds, 8 assists and 4 steals. Imus tumbled to 3-16 despite Darbin's 27 points, 6 rebounds and 2 assists, Ian Pardo's 16 points and 4 assists, and John Calma's 10 points, 9 rebounds and 3 steals. The tournament returns to the One Arena Cainta in Rizal Province on Thursday, featuring games between Manila and Marikina at 3 p.m., Paranaque and Quezon Province at 5 p.m., and Pasig and Negros at 7 p.m.

This Filipina ace has the makings of a future tennis princess. Crystal Saphire Embol is slowly making her own name in the tennis world after clinching two gold medals in the recently concluded State Games of America in State College, Pennsylvania. With Alex Eala already creating noise in the professional scene, Embol turned heads in the biennial meet after ruling the women’s open singles and doubles events where she bested rivals from the states of Colorado, Florida, Pennsylvania, and Virginia. “Hindi ko po inaasahan na makakamit ko ‘to. Pinagtrabahuhan ko lang araw-araw and ‘di ko po sinukuan,” said the 16-year-old Embol, who also served as flag-bearer for Team West Virginia. “Para po ‘to sa aking pamilya, mga coaches, and siyempre para sa Pilipinas,” she added. Before her two-gold haul in the competition, Embol, whose roots come from Misamis Occidental, already reigned in West Virginia’s Women’s Open in the past two years. “Crystal’s outstanding performance has brought national recognition to West Virginia and serves as an inspiration to young athletes across the Mountain State,” the State Games of West Virginia wrote on its social media post. “Her success reflects the power of hard work, perseverance, and the support of family, coaches, sponsors, and the community. She returns home not only as a two-time national champion, but also as a proud ambassador for West Virginia tennis,” it added. Currently unranked in the amateur scene, Embol hopes to reach the WTA level in the future as well as to represent the country on the international stage.

Legit Status Varsity heads to UDO World Finals. The 24-member Legit Status Varsity is set to represent the Philippines at the 2026 UDO World Street Dance Championships in Blackpool, United Kingdom, adding another exciting international chapter to the Filipino dance community’s growing list of achievements. From Aug. 12–16, Blackpool’s iconic Winter Gardens will bring together thousands of dancers from around the world, with the Philippines proudly taking its place on the world stage. The team earned its spot in the Under 18 Team Division after securing first and second place at the UDO Philippines Street Dance Championship in Quezon City from Nov. 21–23, 2025. Following their standout performance, UDO Philippines officially confirmed Legit Status Varsity as a Philippine qualifier and representative for the 2026 UDO World Street Dance Championships in an invitation dated February 6. These young dancers come together from different backgrounds and cities, united by one passion and one goal: to put the Philippines on the global dance map. With each competition, Legit Status continues to make its mark on the international competitive dance scene, building a reputation as the Philippine powerhouse in hip-hop dance. Founded in 2009 under artistic director Vimi Rivera, Legit Status has steadily built a reputation both locally and internationally. Among its biggest breakthroughs came at the 2023 and 2025 World Hip Hop Dance Championships in Phoenix, Arizona, where Legit Status emerged as world champion in the MegaCrew Division. The group’s younger dancers have continued to make their own mark, with Legit Status Varsity earning bronze in the JV MegaCrew Division at the 2025 World Hip Hop Dance Championship. The Varsity team is carrying that momentum into 2026, winning World Champion in the Under 16 category and 1st Runner Up in the Over 18 MegaCrew division in Manchester’s SOAR competition. It is against this backdrop of growing international success that Legit Status Varsity now takes on Blackpool, ready to represent the Philippines on the world stage. Their participation points to something larger happening within Philippine dance: a new generation of performers is entering a competitive scene where Filipino crews have already proven that they can not only qualify for major international competitions, but win them. Legit Status’ success has also earned recognition beyond the dance floor. Following the team’s 2025 World Hip Hop Dance Championship victory, the Philippine Senate formally recognized Legit Status, commending the dancers for bringing pride and international recognition to the country. Now the next generation gets its turn. When Legit Status Varsity takes the floor in Blackpool this August, its 24 young dancers will be competing for a world title of their own — and adding another chapter to a Philippine street dance story that is becoming increasingly difficult for the rest of the world to overlook. Continue to cheer Legit Status Varsity on. As long as the fire burns, the story will always go on. Because when you’re too legit to quit, the only victory you need to overcome is your own.

P1.7-M worth of smuggled cigarettes seized in Batangas. CAMP MIGUEL MALVAR, Batangas City- Police confiscated P1.7 million worth of smuggled cigarettes and arrested a trader during a buy-bust operation on Wednesday night, Aug. 12, in Barangay Poblacion 1, Calaca City, this province. The suspect was identified as MK, 33, a store merchandise owner and resident of the said place. Investigation showed that the suspect was arrested after accepting the marked buy-bust money from a police poseur-buyer in exchange for illicit cigarettes during the operation conducted by joint operatives of the 1st Provincial Intelligence Team–Provincial Intelligence Unit (1st PIT-PIU), BPPO, together with the Calaca Component City Police Station, RID4A, and RSOU, for alleged violations of Section 118(c) of Republic Act No. 10863, or the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA), and Sections 144, 262, and 263 of Republic Act No. 8424, or the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC). Thirty master cases of various brands of cigarettes with a total value of P1,719,000, a multi-purpose van with license plate no. DAV 1936, and marked money were recovered. Alias MK has been placed under the custody of the Batangas Police Provincial Office while appropriate charges were being prepared. The Batangas PPO said it remains firm in its fight against the illicit cigarette trade and continues to protect legitimate businesses, safeguard government revenues, and support the province’s drive for economic security. Col. Oliver Ebora, Batangas police director, said, “We will continue working with our partner units and intensify operations to protect lawful commerce and hold accountable those who choose to profit from illegal activities." He added that the Batangas PPO remains firm in its fight against the illicit cigarette trade to protect legitimate businesses, safeguard government revenues, and support the province’s drive towards economic security.

Senate resolution honors SB19 for taking OPM to Lollapalooza 2026. Senator Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan has filed a resolution congratulating and commending Filipino P-pop supergroup SB19 for becoming the first Filipino act to perform at Lollapalooza, one of the world's largest and most influential music festivals. Filed on Tuesday, August 4, Senate Resolution No. 573 honors SB19's historic performance at Lollapalooza Chicago 2026 and recognizes the group's role in bringing Original Pilipino Music (OPM) to a global audience. The five-member group composed of Pablo, Josh, Stell, Ken, and Justin has been touted as the “Kings of P-Pop.” The group pioneered the modern Filipino idol group movement and made history in 2021 as the first Filipino act nominated at the Billboard Music Awards under Top Social Artist. “Their performance at Lollapalooza is a momentous occasion in celebrating Filipino excellence in music, arts, and dance,” Pangilinan said in the resolution. “It cements the global significance of Original Pilipino Music and highlights the impact of Filipino talent in the performing arts,” he further said. Last July 31, SB19 delivered a high-energy set at the Allianz Stage featuring hits like “GENTO” and “MAPA,” alongside a tribute performance of Francis Magalona's “Mga Kababayan.” SB19 shared the 2026 festival roster with global superstars like Jennie, Lorde, Charli XCX, and Tate McRae, and showcased OPM before a global audience and demonstrated that Filipino artists can stand alongside the world's biggest acts. But beyond their artistic achievements, the senator commended SB19 for their heart for public service. The Senate resolution recognizes the group's philanthropic work, including raising disaster relief funds, donating hospital gear during the COVID-19 pandemic, and supporting various charitable foundations. “There is likely no doubt that Filipino talent in music is world-class. I would be the first to say that our singers are exceptional. As you know—being the husband of the Megastar and having many friends in the industry—I consider myself a true OPM fan,” the senator said. “But above all, I hope this serves as a reminder to our lawmakers that we also have a responsibility to focus on our creative industry, so that more Filipinos may be given the opportunity to showcase their talent to the world,” he added. SRN 573 also reaffirms the importance of supporting Filipino artists whose achievements inspire national pride and strengthen the country’s cultural presence on the world stage. The measure also underscores the need to continue investing in the Philippine creative industries so that more Filipino talent can thrive internationally.

Crowd sweetheart Alex Eala emerges as busiest player on Tour. Alex Eala’s continued rise on the global tennis scene, along with her steady climb in the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) rankings, can be traced to one simple approach: play as much as she can. The 21-year-old Eala turned out to be the busiest player in the women's field after playing 56 matches which include her historic maiden Tour title in the WTA 500 Mubadala D.C. Open in Washington, D.C. Eala, now ranked No. 20, competed more than 50 times since the start of the season, notching 37 wins and 19 defeats with the most recent coming from a 4-6, 0-6 loss to Swiss Belinda Bencic in the Last 16 of the WTA 1000 National Bank Open. Her record includes big wins over high-ranked netters in Americans Jessica Pegula (No. 3) and Coco Gauff (No. 4), Polish Iga Swiatek (No. 8), Ukrainian Elina Svitolina (No. 9), and Kazakh Elena Rybakina (No. 2). Eala now has a 9-4 record against Top 10 players. She also beat former world No. 1 and four-time Grand Slam winner Naomi Osaka of Japan , 6-4, 6-2, in the D.C Open semis. The Southeast Games champion has also beaten all podium finishers in the 2024 Paris Olympics in China’s Zheng Qingwen, Croatian Donna Vekic, and Iga Swiatek. Eala, who soared in the WTA Finals race where she is currently at No. 14. Aside from Eala, Svitolina (52), Pegula (51), Rybakina (50), Mirra Andreeva (50), and German Tatjana Maria (50) were also having hectic calendars. The number of matches Eala has played significantly increased as she gained access to Challenger-level tournaments, particularly WTA 125 events, which are designed for lower-ranked players and generally restrict Top 10 players from entering. Among the WTA 125 tournaments she competed in were the inaugural Philippine Women’s Open and the Birmingham Open, where the 5-foot-9 Filipina captured her second WTA 125 title. The charming lefty is currently preparing for her upcoming campaign as the No. 17 seed in the WTA 1000 Cincinnati Open in Mason, Ohio this week.

3 South Korean divers rescued off Isla Verde in Batangas. BATANGAS CITY- Three South Korean divers were rescued off Isla Verde, Batangas during a diving activity at Canyon Reef, Barangay Sinandigan, Puerto Galera, Oriental Mindoro, on August 11, 2026. Philippine Coast Guard Southern Tagalog reported that the divers were expected to surface after one hour of diving. The report said that when the divers failed to surface within the expected time, the operator of the divers’ speedboat attempted to locate them but was unable to do so due to worsening sea conditions. The operator contacted the municipal administrator of Puerto Galera, who immediately reported the incident to the Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Puerto Galera, prompting the deployment of Search and Rescue (SAR) teams. The CGSS Puerto Galera coordinated with PNP Maritime, MDRRMO Puerto Galera, local dive operators, and other maritime stakeholders to intensify the search for the three foreign divers. The report added that during the search, the three divers were located approximately 3.12 nautical miles northwest of Brgy. San Agustin, Isla Verde, Batangas. The crew of M/V FastCat M19 spotted a rapidly flashing light on the water which led to the location of the divers. One female diver was successfully rescued by M/V FastCat M19, while the two male divers were safely recovered by Paradise Diving Boat 4. The three divers were brought together and safely transported to Brgy. Sabang, Puerto Galera. The foreigners were assessed by personnel of MDRRMO Puerto Galera and confirmed to be in safe condition. The Coast Guard Station (CGS) Oriental Mindoro, in coordination with CGSS Puerto Galera, is conducting further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, including compliance with applicable maritime safety requirements.

S&R membership surge drives Puregold first-semester profit to ₱5.9 billion. Puregold Price Club Inc., one of the largest grocery retailers in the country, reported an 11 percent increase in consolidated net income for the first half of the year on the back of robust sales growth and expanding profit margins. In a regulatory filing with the Philippine Stock Exchange, Puregold said net profit rose to ₱5.87 billion in the first six-months of the year from ₱5.3 billion in the same period last year. Consolidated revenues climbed 10.6 percent to ₱121.48 billion from ₱109.88 billion in the prior-year period. Puregold attributed its financial performance to strong top-line momentum and improved gross margins, which were bolstered by continued support from suppliers. Same-store sales growth, a key metric evaluating performance across existing locations open for at least a year, remained positive across the company’s retail brands. Puregold-branded supermarket stores recorded a 3.7 percent gain in same-store sales, driven by larger average basket sizes per customer. Meanwhile, the membership warehouse chain S&R registered a 13 percent surge in same-store sales, primarily propelled by higher customer foot traffic. The retail group’s consolidated gross profit for the period expanded 13 percent to ₱23.66 billion from ₱20.95 billion recorded in the same period last year. Other operating income rose 5.9 percent to ₱1.97 billion from ₱1.86 billion. Consequently, gross operating income advanced 12.4 percent to ₱25.63 billion from ₱22.81 billion, yielding a gross operating margin of 21 percent. Operating expenses grew 12 percent to ₱16.74 billion from ₱14.99 billion year-on-year, driven by ongoing operational requirements and store network activity. Net other expenses increased to ₱1.24 billion for the first six months from ₱966 million in the corresponding period in 2025. As of the end of June 2026, Puregold operated a nationwide network of 794 retail locations. The company's footprint includes 688 Puregold supermarket stores, 33 S&R Membership shopping warehouses, and 73 S&R New York Style Quick Service Restaurants. (James A. Loyola)

End-July rice imports jump 27% as government builds buffer for El Niño. Rice imports rose by nearly 27 percent year-on-year to more than three million metric tons (MT) in the first seven months, as the country ramped up purchases of foreign supplies to secure adequate stocks ahead of El Niño. The latest Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI) data showed that the country’s rice imports reached 3.27 million MT as of end-July, from 2.58 million MT in the same period last year. The latest import volume puts the country on track to surpass total imports of 3.39 million MT in 2025, when the government imposed a four-month suspension on the entry of foreign-sourced rice. Unlike last year, Department of Agriculture (DA) Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel earlier said there will be no import ban this year in order to prepare for the impact of the extreme El Niño in the fourth quarter of the year. The DA chief said maintaining adequate stocks outweighs the benefits of restricting imports, given the heightened risks from El Niño and its impact on the country’s rice production. Based on the DA’s latest projection, the country’s rice output is on track to decline by around 750,000 MT this year due to El Niño, way higher than its initial projected loss of 700,000 MT. “Our responsibility is to ensure the country has enough buffer stocks well before the next harvest. Food security means being proactive, not reacting after supplies tighten,” Tiu Laurel said in a statement. Instead of a ban, he said the DA is banking on importers to refrain from bringing in five-percent broken rice, or the country’s most commonly consumed imported variety, in favor of 25-percent broken rice or other imported rice with even higher broken-grain percentages. At present, the DA is still waiting on the findings of the Tariff Commission (TC) on whether there is a need to impose a definitive safeguard measure on imported rice. The TC is currently investigating the matter in response to the DA’s probe that found that there is a causal link between increased rice imports and serious injury to the domestic industry. The DA recommended in its findings that the current 15-percent tariff on rice imports be raised by at least 13 percentage points (ppt), bringing the minimum tariff rate to 28 percent. It noted that the tariff hike should be limited to the country’s principal sources of imported rice, which include Vietnam, Thailand, Pakistan, and Myanmar. BPI data showed that Vietnam remains the top rice supplier as of end-July, with imports reaching 2.53 million MT, or 77 percent of the total volume. The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) estimated in a report that the Philippines accounted for 48 percent of Vietnam’s rice exports in the first half, about 14 percent higher than in the same period last year. Other top sources of rice include Thailand with 343,227 MT, Myanmar with 233,922 MT, Cambodia with 80,678 MT, and Pakistan with 68,313 MT.

Caregiver steals over P594K in cash, jewelry from elderly employer. A female caregiver was arrested in Makati City on Wednesday, Aug. 12, after allegedly stealing cash from her 77-year-old employer by replacing it with a bundle of blank white paper wrapped in scotch tape. The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) said the victim’s family discovered the theft inside their home in Barangay San Antonio at around 7 a.m. The 77-year-old victim is also a person with a disability. Based on the investigation, the theft was uncovered after the victim’s family checked his bag and found that an envelope originally containing cash had been tampered with. Instead of money, the envelope contained a bundle of blank white paper meticulously cut and wrapped in scotch tape to mimic the thickness and form of actual currency. The stolen items included P294,787 in cash plus a gold bracelet and ring worth P300,000. The family confronted the suspect, who reportedly broke down and admitted to the theft. She later transferred P15,000 to the family via GCash and surrendered her iPhone as partial restitution. However, most of the stolen cash and both pieces of jewelry remain unrecovered. This prompted the family to report her to authorities, leading to her arrest for qualified theft at around 8:40 p.m. the same day. The NCRPO said the suspect is undergoing inquest proceedings at the Makati City Police Station while authorities complete the formal charges and documents. NCRPO director Maj. Gen. Anthony A. Aberin emphasized that the case underscores the importance of due diligence when hiring caregivers and other household workers, especially in homes with elderly or PWD family members.

Palace calls out TUPAD beneficiaries over alleged fake cleanup photos, videos. Malacañang has called out some beneficiaries of the government's emergency employment program for allegedly posing as cleaners of waterways for photos and videos while failing to perform the work for which they were hired. Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said this after President Marcos himself said the country is facing a serious garbage problem following flooding in Metro Manila during the recent Habagat rains. In a press briefing on Thursday, Aug. 13, Castro said the reported fake photos and videos of Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) beneficiaries were particularly disappointing because they are paid to perform actual community work, including debris clearing and the declogging of canals. “Ito ay isang example lamang po. Yung mga hina-hire para sa TUPAD, sila ay in-engage para maglinis. Pero nakita po natin na ito ay nag-viral na yung iba ay magpapa-picture lang—kunwari may basurang winalis, pero after that ay aalis na rin (This is just one example: Those hired under TUPAD are engaged to clean, but we saw that some of them went viral for merely having their pictures taken—as if they had swept garbage—but after that, they would leave),” she said. “Minsan sila pa ang nagtatambak ng basura para ipakitang may basura sa lugar. Wawalisin nila and then after that, nandoon lang (Sometimes they are even the ones who pile up the garbage to make it appear that there is trash in the area. They sweep it, and then after that, they just leave it there),” she added. Castro said beneficiaries should fulfill their obligations instead of using government-funded work to produce what she described as fake videos, adding that the program was intended to provide temporary income while addressing community needs. “Ang gobyerno ay binibigay po ang lahat, kayo po ay hina-hire para kahit papano ay meron kayong mapagkakitaan. Pero gawin niyo po ang inyong obligasyon dahil hindi po naman kayo hina-hire at binabayaran para gumawa lang ng fake videos (The government is providing everything; you are hired so that, at the very least, you have a source of income. But do your obligation because you are not being hired and paid just to make fake videos),” she said. The TUPAD program is a Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) emergency employment program that provides temporary work to disadvantaged or displaced workers, including those who are underemployed, displaced, or affected by seasonal employment and other circumstances that disrupt their livelihood. The program covers community-based work such as cleaning and maintaining public facilities, clearing debris, declogging canals, segregating waste, and clearing waterways, making it one of the government's mechanisms for providing short-term income while addressing local community needs. TUPAD beneficiaries are paid based on the prevailing minimum wage in their locality for the duration of their approved work, subject to program requirements and validated attendance. Marcos orders Baclaran River cleanup Before this, President Marcos inspected the Redemptorist Water Channel in Baclaran River on Wednesday, Aug. 12, after successive rains in Metro Manila caused large amounts of garbage to accumulate in the waterway. The President immediately ordered the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) to clear the garbage, with the Parañaque City government also assisting in the cleanup. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), through its Estero Rangers, and TUPAD beneficiaries were likewise mobilized to help remove waste from the waterways. Castro said the cleanup of portions of the river was completed within hours, helping restore water flow and reduce the risk of severe flooding. Marcos also inspected waste collection operations at the Diokno Pumping Station in Pasay City, where he stressed that government cleanup efforts must be matched by responsible waste disposal by the public. Malacañang renewed its appeal to citizens to practice proper waste disposal. “Sa ating mga kababayan, patuloy ang pagtatrabaho ng gobyerno; nililinis po ang ating kapaligiran — huwag ninyo naman pong laging dumihan (To our fellow citizens, the government continues to work and clean our environment—please do not keep dirtying it),” Castro said. Government expands waste-management efforts Castro said the administration is also studying waste-to-energy projects as part of efforts to address the country's waste-disposal requirements. She said the DENR has installed 196 trash traps in Metro Manila to collect floating debris from rivers and waterways and has mobilized about 1,500 estero rangers and river warriors for cleanup and waste-collection activities. DENR Environmental Monitoring Officers will also conduct daily monitoring of unclean sites and notify barangays when cleanup is needed, while the government's Adopt an Estero program already has 20 active private-sector adopters, Castro said. Marcos has also stressed that clearing waterways should be accompanied by sustained declogging and desilting operations under Oplan Kontra Baha. Castro said the government could provide programs and resources, but their effectiveness would still depend on public cooperation in preventing waterways from being used as dumping grounds. She urged Filipinos to work with local governments, barangays, and communities to keep rivers and other waterways clean. “Magkaisa po tayo para sa ating bansa (Let us unite for our country),” she said.

DMAP reveals keynote speakers, conference tracks for DigiCon 2026. The Digital Marketing Association of the Philippines (DMAP) officially kicked off the next phase of DigiCon 2026 with the announcement of its first global keynote speakers, conference tracks, and new partnership opportunities during the DigiCon 2026 Press Conference held on Monday, August 10. Following the earlier reveal of this year's theme, "Interoperability: Welcome to the Age of Collaboration," the media conference offered a first look at how the country's premier digital marketing conference will bring that vision to life through its speaker lineup, conference programming, and industry initiatives leading up to the event. Opening the program, DMAP Vice President for Internal Affairs and Board Trustee Kit Ramos Disini welcomed members of the media and industry partners, emphasizing DigiCon's role in bringing together the marketing ecosystem. "The pace of change in marketing has never been faster, and no one organization has all the answers. DigiCon exists to create the space where brands, agencies, platforms, creators, and innovators can learn from one another and build the future together,” she said. DigiCon 2026 Co-Chair Raymund Sison shared the conference's vision and what attendees can expect from this year's edition. "This is only the beginning of what we'll be unveiling over the coming months. From additional speakers and DigiConX activations to new industry partnerships, we're building a conference that reflects the collaborative future we're asking the industry to embrace,” said Sison. For this year’s edition, DigiCon will include exciting new features to maximize participation and engagement. Breaking from traditional conference boundaries, delegates can look forward to connecting with peers, local creators, and potential partners through networking sessions on the community stage. Delegates can also gain insights from industry leaders during keynote sessions, build practical skills in hands-on workshops, and explore immersive brand activations. Among the day's major announcements was the confirmation of the first two international keynote speakers for DigiCon 2026. Professor Dr. Christian Busch, bestselling author of Connect the Dots and professor at the University of Southern California and the London School of Economics, shared a video message previewing his keynote on how organizations can unlock innovation by building meaningful connections across industries and embracing serendipity as a competitive advantage. Joining him is Judy John, Global Chief Creative Officer of Edelman and one of the world's most awarded creative leaders. In her video message, John spoke about the importance of cross-disciplinary thinking as brands navigate increasingly interconnected audiences, platforms, and technologies. The press conference also introduced the tracks for DigiCon 2026. In a panel discussion moderated by Director for Publicity Mori Rodriguez, Track Leads Gino Nacianceno (Innovation), Jordan Santos (Impact), and Denise Haak (Immersive), together with DigiConX Co-Director Nikki Sunga, shared the conversations shaping this year's program. The discussion explored how organizations can move beyond AI hype to real business value, create immersive experiences through cross-sector partnerships, build authentic purpose-driven campaigns, and transform audiences from passive consumers into active collaborators. This year, DMAP is also pioneering DigiConX, a nationwide expansion of the conference experience through a series of satellite pop-ups across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Ahead of the main conference, DigiConX brings the industry's biggest conversations closer to communities by partnering with organizations, schools, and brands to host talks, panels, and learning sessions across the country. More than just a roadshow, DigiConX extends the reach and impact of DigiCon, empowering local communities to connect, collaborate, and shape the future of digital marketing. Closing the event, Director for Creative & Experience Dale Lopez and Partnerships & Sponsorship Lead Alan Fontanilla unveiled the new DigiCon website and announced sponsorship and partnership opportunities. The DigiCon 2026 Press Conference was held in partnership with Astoria Hotels and Resorts, the official venue partner for the event. DigiCon 2026 will take place on October 15–16, 2026, at the Grand Ballroom of the Manila Marriott Hotel. Organizations interested in sponsorships and partnerships may also inquire through digicon@futureproof.ph. For tickets, announcements, speaker reveals, and key event highlights, visit DigiCon’s official website and social media channels.

Koreans' firepower overwhelms Alas Girls. LOS ANDES, Chile -- The Philippines matched Korea in grit, but not in firepower, dropping an entertaining Round of 16 match, 25-21, 25-18, 25-14, on Wednesday in the FIVB Volleyball Girls U17 World Championship on Wednesday, Aug. 12. With Xyz Rayco’s steady play and Caera Celis’s persistent offense, Alas Pilipinas Girls held slim leads in several instances at the Liceo Mixto Los Andes. The Philippines managed to apply some pressure with timely attacks and showed improved cohesion during extended rallies, but Korea was simply superior in delivering sharp attacks out of scrambling sequences. While Alas Pilipinas—supported by the Philippine Olympic Committee, Philippine Sports Commission and Asics—kept it close in blocks, 5-7, and hit four aces against six, the Koreans’ ability to score off-system gave them a 45-29 advantage in attacks. Soyeon Son had 19 points, including 13 attacks, while Minseo Eo scored 15, with 14 coming from attacks as Korea advanced to the quarterfinals against Turkiye, which swept Japan, 25-18, 25-7, 25-23. Celis again paced the Philippines with 14 points on12 attacks, a block and an ace, while Rayco had a near all-around performance, scoring nine and contributing on defense. The Philippines gears up for battle against Japan in the playoffs for 9th to 16th on Thursday in the capital city Santiago after the tournament break on Wednesday. In Santiago, Thailand pulled off the upset of the tournament so far as the Asian power that underachieved in pool play with a 2-3 win-loss record in Pool A turned back Pool C winner Poland, 25-19, 25-21, 10-25, 25-23. China, meanwhile, suffered its first dropped set of the tournament, overcoming a stiff challenge from the Dominican Republic, 25-18, 17-25, 25-19, 25-17, in San Felipe. Chinese Taipei routed Venezuela, 25-21, 25-19, 25-22, making it four Asian teams in the final eight. The USA extended its streak without dropping a set, defeating Argentina, 25-15, 25-23, 25-15. Italy marched on with a 25-13, 25-11, 25-13 drubbing of Peru, while Croatia rolled past Czechia 25-21, 25-21, 25-19.

BOC courts energy, automotive, food giants for elite importers office. Twenty-four leading importers have already engaged with the Bureau of Customs (BOC) over the creation of an elite importer group, including energy giants Petron Corp. and Shell Pilipinas Corp., as well as major players in the aviation, automotive, food, and manufacturing industries. This comes as the BOC eyes the rollout of its Top Importers Office (TIO) by the third quarter of 2026, which Manila Bulletin earlier reported would be composed of a maximum of 2,000 major importers whose taxes make up roughly three-fourths of the bureau’s annual haul. According to the BOC, Customs Commissioner Ariel F. Nepomuceno held the bureau’s consultations with stakeholders, engaging with leading energy and petroleum firms, including Petron, Insular Oil Corp., Shell Pilipinas, Chevron Philippines Inc., Seaoil, Unioil, and Jetti Petroleum. Major players in the aviation, automotive, technology, food, healthcare, and manufacturing industries were also consulted, including Philippine Airlines (PAL), Mitsubishi, Suzuki Philippines, HP PPS Philippines, Coca-Cola Europacific Aboitiz Philippines (CCEAP), Mondelez, Monde Nissin Corp., Century Pacific Food Inc. (CNPF), Golden Arches Development Corp. (GADC), Mondo Cucina, Wills International, IE Medica, Medethix, Lifeline Diagnostics Supplies, Concepcion Durables, Concepcion-Carrier, and SCG Marketing. Overall, the BOC has engaged with at least 24 major importers potentially securing their spots in the elite group. Headed by BOC Director George JT D. Aliño II, TIO was established to serve as a “strategic link to foster seamless collaboration between key trade partners and the bureau’s operational units,” acting as the primary point of contact for the country’s high-volume traders. During the initial consultation sessions held in July, the BOC formally introduced TIO as a “central coordinating hub” intended to promote a more efficient and reliable trading environment. It was during the consultations that industry leaders had a chance to voice pressing challenges in their respective industries. “Company representatives raised specific operational concerns involving import clearances, processing delays, and inter-office coordination,” the BOC said. In response, TIO has already launched structured assistance and tracking mechanisms to ensure that these issues are systematically routed to the appropriate BOC offices for “timely evaluation and action.” Nepomuceno said TIO “will serve as our direct bridge to key stakeholders, making our coordination faster and clearer.” “Through open dialogue, we will not only respond to operational issues, but we will also identify the root cause of problems to provide lasting solutions,” Nepomuceno added. Building the office aligns with the BOC’s push for integrity, accountability, and modernization. - Derco Rosal

Alternergy wins high credit rating for planned ₱2-billion note issue. Renewable energy firm Alternergy Holdings Corp. is planning to raise ₱2 billion from a planned issuance of Fixed-Rate Corporate Notes, which have been given a very strong investment grade rating by Philippine Rating Services Corporation (PhilRatings). PhilRatings said it has assigned an investment grade Issue Credit Rating of "PRS Aa minus," with a Stable Outlook, to Alternergy's proposed note issuance. “Proceeds from the issue will be used by the Company for advancing predevelopment expenses of its projects awarded by the Department of Energy (DOE) under the fourth round of its Green Energy Auction Program (GEAP-4) and other projects in the Company’s pipeline and for general corporate purposes, including the full payment of its loans,” the ratings firm said. Obligations rated PRS Aa are of high quality and subject to very low credit risk, with the obligor’s capacity to meet its financial commitment on the obligation considered very strong. The “minus” further qualifies the rating, while a Stable Outlook indicates that the rating is likely to be maintained over the next 12 months. The assigned rating and corresponding Outlook took into account Alternergy’s growing renewable energy portfolio supported by a favorable industry outlook, albeit limited in size and scale relative to the broader industry. PhilRatings also considered the firm’s competent and well-experienced shareholders and management team; its pioneer status in clean energy innovation; its recovering bottom line after recording a net loss in 2022, supported by upcoming projects with long-term off-take contracts; and its increasing leverage levels to support growth. With a combined installed capacity of 119 megawatts (MW) as of end-March 2026, Alternergy’s operational portfolio spans the Philippines and the Republic of Palau. The company has 11 solar projects (eight of which are under one rooftop portfolio), one wind farm, and one mini run-of-river hydro project. Looking ahead, Alternergy’s growth in scale and capacity will be supported by the DOE’s push to increase the share of renewable energy in the country’s overall power generation mix to 35 percent by 2030 and 50 percent by 2040. Power projects awarded under the second round of the Green Energy Auction Program (GEAP-2)—the Tanay and Alabat Wind Projects—are in the advanced stages of construction and are expected to commence operations by October 2026. These are projected to increase Alternergy’s operating capacity to 311 MW by end-2026. The company’s projects under GEAP-4—Liberty Solar, Kalandagan Solar, Alegria Wind, and Tayabas North Wind—are under development and are expected to be completed and begin operations in the next three years. Projects in the pipeline have a combined potential capacity of 762 MW. To fund its growth, Alternergy has tapped the capital markets and banks. Consequently, its consolidated debt-to-equity ratio moved from 0.6 times as of calendar year-end 2021 to 3.0 times as of fiscal year-end 2025, driven by additional debt drawdowns to fund the construction of its capital-intensive power projects. As of end-March 2026, the debt-to-equity ratio increased to 4.1 times. At the parent level, the debt-to-equity ratio stood at 1.0 times as of fiscal year-end 2025.

Marcos orders inclusion of contract-of-service and job-order workers in social protection coverage. President Marcos has ordered the inclusion of contract-of-service (COS) and job-order (JO) workers in the government’s social protection coverage. Marcos issued Administrative Order No. 43, facilitating the voluntary deduction and remittance of Social Security System (SSS), Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), and Pag-IBIG Fund Contributions of COS and JO workers in government. “All covered government agencies are hereby directed to facilitate the voluntary deduction of prescribed SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG Fund contributions from the compensation of COS and JO workers, subject to the prior consent of the worker and in accordance with RA Nos. 11199, 11223, and 9679,” Marcos stated in the order dated June 3. “For this purpose, agencies shall ensure that appropriate mechanisms are in place to enable participation and shall provide COS and JO workers with the necessary information on available social protection coverage,” the order added. The order covers all departments, agencies, bureaus, offices, and instrumentalities of the national government, including government-owned or -controlled corporations (GOCCs) and state universities and colleges (SUCs), engaging the services of individual COS and JO workers. Local government units (LGUs) are also encouraged to observe the provisions of Administrative Order No. 43. According to the order, concerned agencies shall remit the deducted contributions directly to the SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG Fund, ensure the timely remittance of such contributions, and execute the necessary agreements with the concerned institutions to facilitate proper implementation. The facilitation of voluntary deduction and remittance provided for in AO 43 shall not alter, amend, or modify the existing contractual relationship between government agencies and their COS or JO workers, it further stated. The Department of Budget and Management (DBM), Civil Service Commission (CSC), Commission on Audit (COA), SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG Fund were directed to jointly issue the necessary rules, guidelines, and accounting procedures to ensure the effective implementation of the order. Joint Circular No. 1 (s. 2025) issued by the CSC, COA, and DBM provides that COS and JO workers may be granted a premium, not exceeding 20 percent of their compensation, to cover voluntary or self-employed contributions to government-mandated social security programs.

Japan testing new tech to prevent heatstroke among elderly. Tokyo (Jiji Press) -- Japan's Environment Ministry has launched a demonstration experiment to help protect elderly people from heatstroke by utilizing artificial intelligence and sensors to encourage them to use air conditioners properly. The initiative aims to identify heatstroke risks proactively as extreme heat continues to claim the lives of many elderly people indoors. The demonstration test features three programs--an AI-based system that estimates core body temperatures and notifies users of the risk of heatstroke via a smartwatch, a monitoring system that notifies registered family members through an app when indoor temperatures exceed certain levels and a system that automatically activates air conditioners based on room temperatures. The test uses commercially available products developed mainly by medical device manufacturers. It began in June, covering 60 to 70 participants aged 65 and older. The trial is expected to continue for about four months, through September. If the systems prove effective, the ministry plans to provide support for their adoption in earnest beginning in fiscal 2027. The test will assess the frequency of malfunctions and errors in using air conditioners, as well as whether the technology encourages preventive action, such as turning on air conditioners or moving to cooler places. The ministry will also conduct a survey examining elderly people's psychological resistance to new technology, as many of them are reluctant to use air conditioners. According to the ministry, elderly people accounted for about 85 pct of heatstroke fatalities in 2024, with most deaths occurring at home. Many elderly people and those with pre-existing health conditions may have a reduced ability to sense heat and thirst, while family members and caregivers may recognize warning signs too late. The ministry aims to strengthen effective heatstroke prevention efforts through new technology amid increasing numbers of elderly people living alone and worsening shortages of caregivers.

Japan's law against national flag vandalism takes effect. TOKYO, Aug. 13 (Jiji Press) -- A law to criminalize acts of damaging Japan's national flag came into effect Thursday, amid unresolved concerns about its impact on expressive activities following criticisms that the scope of punishable acts is unclear. Under the Japanese law, those who publicly damage, remove or deface the national flag in a way that causes people to feel extremely uncomfortable or disgusted could face up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 200,000 yen. Livestreams of such acts are subject to punishment, while archive broadcasts are not. The law seeks to protect tangible objects used as a national flag. Creative works, such as anime and images produced with generative artificial intelligence, as well as flag-shaped decorations on children's meals and flag-inspired patterns on clothes are excluded from the scope of the law. The legislation stipulates that whether an act is punishable is determined through a comprehensive assessment of the objective circumstances, including the external form of the act and the surrounding situation, while giving consideration to the freedom of expression and belief. In parliamentary deliberations on the law before its enactment on July 17, the interpretation of "extremely uncomfortable" was a major issue. Opponents argued that the abstract language could restrict artistic expression and political activities. Earlier this month, the Justice Ministry set up a page on its website explaining the law. It says that "ways causing strong discomfort from the perspective of ordinary members of the public are considered to be methods that make people feel extremely uncomfortable," and shows examples presented to the Diet, or parliament, by lawmakers who sponsored the legislation, including those from the ruling Liberal Democratic Party. Among the examples, burning flags in front of train stations, defiling flags with feces or urine, and placing flags on public roads to deface them with mud and rain are cited as acts making people feel extremely uncomfortable. Meanwhile, intentionally hitting golf balls designed like the Japanese flag into the water on golf courses, punching flags with one's bare hands and burning old flags for disposal are not classified as such acts. Criminalizing flag-damaging acts, a key policy goal for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, also LDP president, was included in the coalition agreement between the party and its ally, the Japan Innovation Party. Constitutional scholars who testified in Diet meetings raised concerns about the law, arguing that it is unconstitutional.

Takaichi unlikely to visit Yasukuni Shrine on war anniversary. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is expected to skip a visit to Tokyo's war-related Yasukuni Shrine on Saturday, the anniversary of the country's surrender in World War II, people familiar with the matter said Wednesday. She is apparently considering the need to maintain good relations with South Korea and smooth the way for diplomatic events in the months to come, including the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to be held in China in November. The Shinto shrine is regarded by neighboring Asian countries such as South Korea and China as a symbol of Japan's wartime militarism, as it honors Class-A war criminals along with the nation's war dead. Takaichi is unlikely to visit Yasukuni Shrine "because doing so could complicate relations with South Korea," a person close to the prime minister said. Japanese and South Korean leaders regularly meet through so-called shuttle diplomacy. Takaichi hosted South Korean President Lee Jae-myung for talks in her home prefecture of Nara in January, while she visited Andong, Lee's hometown, for a meeting in May. "If the prime minister visits Yasukuni Shrine, the president would feel betrayed. That could trigger a shift away from the current positive momentum in Japan-South Korea relations," a person familiar with diplomatic relations between the two countries said. Additionally, Takaichi faces a busy diplomatic schedule beginning this autumn, including delivering a speech at the U.N. General Assembly and participating in the Group of 20 summit. In particular, attention is growing over whether Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping will meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit as relations between the two countries have been strained since the Japanese leader's remarks about a potential Taiwan conflict last November. Asked about the possibility of a Japan-China summit at a press conference on July 27, Takaichi said only, "I look forward to the APEC summit." A visit to Yasukuni Shrine by the prime minister would almost certainly draw a strong reaction from China and pose a significant obstacle to holding a Takaichi-Xi summit. Another likely reason for skipping a visit to Yasukuni Shrine is that U.S. President Donald Trump's administration is worried about worsening Japan-China relations. In July, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that he was concerned about ties between the countries. The United States expressed disappointment when then Prime Minister Shinzo Abe visited the shrine in 2013. Takaichi "will not visit the shrine this time. We need to create an environment for this in advance," a lawmaker in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party close to her said. She previously visited Yasukuni Shrine on Aug. 15 every year. Since taking office as prime minister in October last year, she has not visited the shrine.

Punishing European drought shrivels crops from Dutch potatoes to Bosnian corn. WOLPHAARTSDIJK, Netherlands (AP) — A cloud of dust billows behind Maarten Janse’s tractor as he spreads a mixture of compost, straw and manure over a field to nourish the parched soil. Janse's farm on the fertile land of the Netherlands' southwestern Zeeland Province is drying out despite his efforts to make it more drought resistant as accelerated human-caused global warming and a supersized El Nino batter fields across Europe. The drought that is roasting much of Europe this summer is taking a heavy toll on crops across the continent, from potatoes in the Netherlands to corn in Bosnia and grapes in Italy. Even when farmers try to adapt, the extreme weather is hitting their crops and water supplies. Triodos, a Dutch bank that has a focus on sustainability, published an analysis this week that estimated the heatwaves and drought could reduce gross domestic product across the European Union by 1% for 2026 or around 180 billion euros ($208 billion). Farmers are among the hardest hit, with their crops set to be badly affected by soaring temperatures and lack of water. In large parts of the Netherlands, farmers are no longer allowed to use water from streams and drainage channels to irrigate fields and orchards. Just add water? Dutch crops suffer from the drought Another farmer in Zeeland, Hendrik Jan ten Cate, looks at a field full of withered potato plants that are almost all ready for harvest — a month early and with a significantly reduced crop. His potatoes are used to make French fries for companies including McDonald’s, but they’re likely going to be too small this year. “People want long fries,” he says as he holds one of the potatoes. “That’s going to be tough this year.” Ten Cate is one of the lucky farmers because he is allowed to irrigate his crops. But, even so, he estimates his harvest this year will be down by about one-third compared to average years. “It's not just the drought that is the problem," he says. "It is also the sun, the dry air and especially the hot days we have had this year. The potatoes just can't handle that combination very well.” Bosnian agriculture, a key driver of the economy, is suffering In Bosnia, where agriculture contributes roughly 5% of annual GDP and 10% of all employment, grain farmer Slavisa Lukic stood in one of his corn fields as stalks blew limply in the breeze. His crops have been hit by repeated heat waves and drought conditions. He said this year’s corn yield would be very poor, if he manages to harvest one at all. Lukic remembers when he grew 6 to 7 tons per hectare on his farm. He expects this year’s corn yield will be around 1.5 to 2 tons per hectare. Pointing to the drought-stricken land in northeastern Bosnia, Lukic said clover fields that once grew abundantly have all but disappeared. “Now they literally do not exist,” he said. “Nothing.” Czech brewers fear bad hop harvest The drought is even hitting one of the Czech Republic's most famous products: beer. Plzeňský Prazdroj, the country’s largest beer producer, expects to incur losses this year due to a stunted hops yield. Jakub Zaoral, the brewer’s sustainability manager, said that changes in rainfall patterns – characterized by long periods of dryness with occasional heavy storms – mean that when rain does fall, it runs off the dry soil. That results in inconsistent yields and increasingly low groundwater levels. “There’s no choice but to simply accept the fact that one year will be great and the next won’t be,” he said. “If it were to happen three times in a row, that could very well become an existential problem for hop growers.” Drought takes a toll across the Danube region In Romania, some heat and drought-resistant crops like sunflowers have been less affected by the extreme conditions and yields have been plentiful. But the drought is still hitting home with record-low water levels on the Danube River disrupting grain transport, causing chronically congested terminals and an increasing pileup of crops with nowhere to go. “In a short time, maximum 10 days, we will enter full blast in sunflower harvest, to be followed by corn,” Cezar Gheorghe, founder of grain consultancy firm Agricolumn, told The Associated Press. “Already farmers are in panic mode. They can’t find a place to store the corn and sunflower seeds.” Cattle grazing plains in Hungary are turning to dust. No rain has fallen on Sándor Molnár's dairy farm since late May and he is having to buy expensive feed for his 130 cows. “We’re trying to hang in there and hope for the best, hoping next year will be better,” he added. “To be honest, we’ve been saying that for a few years now, but maybe this time it will be.” Huge UK farm that invested in irrigation is feeling the heat Elveden Estate, with more than 10,000 acres of farmland on the Suffolk-Norfolk border in eastern England, has built a reservoir that can hold enough water to fill about 200 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Less than a year after opening, it's almost dry. Another reservoir is at about 20% capacity. But the farm's water policy is paying off. "The fact that we’ve invested significantly in reservoir storage and the infrastructure associated with pumping water has meant that we’ve been in a very strong position to continue to irrigate our crops through this growing season,” the farm's managing director, Andrew Blenkiron, said. But every drop counts. “We’re very concerned that we haven’t got enough water to see us through this season," Blenkiron said. “We’ve got probably, if this weather stays as it is, six weeks of watering left to do.” Diversify and feed the soil Janse uses no-till farming on his fields — not plowing the soil, planting crops to cover the ground year-round and adding organic matter — to help cope with the whims of the weather as climate change triggers more extremes. He has also diversified by running a popular campsite on his farm near the picturesque town of Veere. As he tends to his fields, guests walk by toward a lake where yachts and a river cruise ship sail past. And as dry weather causes an increase in soil salinity in fields, Janse grows samphire, also known as sea asparagus, on a small patch of land. It's a crop that can thrive in salty conditions. But with no rainfall, even that is struggling this year. “Samphire needs fresh water, and if there is only saltwater it doesn’t grow either,” he said.

Millions crowd Spanish cities to see country's first total solar eclipse in over a century. MEDINACELI, Spain (AP) — Millions of people crowded cloudless cities and towns in Spain on Wednesday in search of the best views of a total solar eclipse, when the alignment of the sun, moon and Earth briefly plunged parts of the planet into darkness. The crowds brought lawn chairs and umbrellas as they eagerly awaited the celestial spectacle, which began early in the evening. As the sky darkened, gradually at first and then quickly, people broke into applause and cheered. It was the country's first total solar eclipse in more than a century. “It’s simply impossible to imagine,” Rosa Celiberti, a language teacher who watched from Medinaceli, a Roman-era hilltop town in northeast Spain, said with tears in her eyes. “No matter how many photos or videos you’ve seen, nothing comes even close to what it actually feels like." Across a wide band of northern and central Spain and Portugal, millions of people enjoyed some of mainland Europe's best views of the eclipse. It also passed over slivers of Greenland and Iceland. Totality — when the moon completely covers the sun’s light — was expected to last less than 2½ minutes, reaching its maximum duration off Iceland’s west coast. By the time it got to a small patch of Portugal and then to Spain, just before sunset, totality dwindled to a minute or so. The total eclipse then ended over the Mediterranean. The eclipse was expected to draw at least a half-million additional visitors, Spanish authorities said. Demand for hotel rooms along the path of totality, including in the northern cities of A Coruña, Bilbao and Santiago de Compostela, soared. Rural areas prepared for an influx of visitors The event unfolded against the backdrop of scorching summer temperatures and wildfires, and Spanish officials rolled out a large public safety campaign. Temperatures across much of Spain climbed above 35 degrees Celsius (95 Fahrenheit) in many areas where the eclipse was observed. Some 350 official viewing sites were set up across the sparsely populated interior, and more than 33,500 law enforcement officers were deployed to observation areas and access points, the Interior Ministry said. Only weeks ago, the most destructive wildfire in Spanish history devoured 500 square kilometers (193 square miles) and forced the evacuation of tens of thousands of people in Ávila, in central Spain. Several smaller wildfires remain active elsewhere in southern and central parts of the country. Despite clouds, sky watchers in Iceland witnessed darkness In Reykjavik, clouds did not prevent hundreds of people from gathering in bright raincoats in front of the landmark Hallgrímskirkja church as the skies darkened. With rain falling, the disk of the sun was barely perceptible and then, suddenly, the lights went out. Only the glow of phones held aloft could be seen. The crowd cheered the darkness as it rained harder and roared even louder when the first light returned. They did not wait to watch the remainder of the partial eclipse and quickly cleared out of the square. Eclipse glasses sold fast Special eclipse glasses were essential for safe viewing, even if only a sliver of the sun remained visible. The glasses are made with special filters that block solar radiation that can damage the eyes. For months, supermarkets, department stores, museums and planetariums across Spain had sold or distributed the glasses, with many pharmacies running out of stock ahead of Wednesday. On Tuesday evening in downtown Madrid, a long line formed outside a photo shop where a sign read, “We carry eclipse glasses.” One woman emerged triumphantly and reassured those waiting: “He has boxes and boxes of them!” A ship circles waters near Greenland hoping to catch a glimpse Sverre Rud, captain of the MS Spitsbergen, was circling the waters of Rypefjord in eastern Greenland trying to make sure he was perfectly positioned for his 126 passengers to view the spectacle. All day, people came up to Rud to ask if he had nailed the right spot, with no clouds. “I will do my best," Rud said. “I will pull out my superman powers." The eclipse may have been startling for the passengers, who had been experiencing 24 hours of daylight on a 17-day cruise in locations mostly north of the Arctic Circle. Suddenly, for two minutes it was dark. Even so, the mood on the polar ship had been pure anticipation. “Everyone is very enthusiastic,” Rud said. “When we were down for breakfast earlier, it was almost like a little bit of a Christmas Eve feeling here." Hotel costs skyrocketed in Spain and Iceland Rooms in Reykjavík, Iceland's capital, averaged more than $1,000 for Wednesday night as Icelanders prepared for their first total solar eclipse since 1954 and the first visible from the capital since 1433. Prices were roughly double 2025 rates, according to data group Lighthouse Intelligence. Many tourists made bookings years in advance. But cloudy skies prevailed across much of the island.
